diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
index c52eccc1621d..aa692b13b6f3 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/hisilicon/hns3/hns3_ethtool.c
@@ -908,9 +908,11 @@ static struct hns3_enet_ring *hns3_backup_ringparam(struct hns3_nic_priv *priv)
 	if (!tmp_rings)
 		return NULL;
 
-	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++) {
 		memcpy(&tmp_rings[i], priv->ring_data[i].ring,
 		       sizeof(struct hns3_enet_ring));
+		tmp_rings[i].skb = NULL;
+	}
 
 	return tmp_rings;
 }
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `hns3_ethtool.c`**
   - A modification was made in the `hns3_backup_ringparam` function.
   - The loop that copies ring data now includes an additional line that sets `tmp_rings[i].skb` to `NULL` for each ring being copied. This change ensures that the `skb` pointer in the backup ring structure is initialized to `NULL`, which helps prevent double free issues when the ring parameters are changed.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `hns3_ethtool.c` addresses a bug related to double freeing of memory when changing the ring parameters in the HNS3 driver. By initializing the `skb` pointer to `NULL`, the patch prevents the system from attempting to free an already freed pointer, which was causing the system to panic. This change is crucial for maintaining the integrity of memory management within the driver, particularly during operations that modify the ring parameters.

        The bug is caused by the double freeing of memory associated with the `skb` pointer in the ring structure when the ring parameters are changed.  static struct hns3_enet_ring *hns3_backup_ringparam(struct hns3_nic_priv *priv)
 {
 	struct hnae3_handle *handle = priv->ae_handle;
 	struct hns3_enet_ring *tmp_rings;
 	int i;
 
 	tmp_rings = kcalloc(handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2,
 			    sizeof(struct hns3_enet_ring), GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!tmp_rings)
 		return NULL;
 
-	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < handle->kinfo.num_tqps * 2; i++) {
 		memcpy(&tmp_rings[i], priv->ring_data[i].ring,
 		       sizeof(struct hns3_enet_ring));
+		tmp_rings[i].skb = NULL;
+	}
 
 	return tmp_rings;
 }
